A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPE-BR sequential pricing study. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and inconsistencies in simulation labels.

before.justification: Section 7 and Figure 2 report original simulations measuring parameter estimation, demand estimation, convergence to Nash equilibrium, and cumulative regret.

after.justification: Section 7 and the revised Figure 2 report original simulations of the same pricing algorithm, including estimation errors, equilibrium distances, and regret.

M1.justification: The estimation stages and best-response procedure remain unchanged. v2 corrects the own-price coefficient's sign and adds the missing price multiplier in Equation (10), bringing these expressions into agreement with Algorithm 1 and Appendix E already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic sequential price competition with Gaussian-CDF demand functions. Seller counts and price sensitivities change within this retained task; no dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario is added.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically compares SPE-BR against competing pricing algorithms. The full-information regret benchmark and Nash-equilibrium reference remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 7 changes stated seller counts from {2,5,8} to {2,4,6} and price sensitivities from [0.71,0.915,0.97] to [0.71,0.92,0.96]. Figure 2 instead labels v1's rows {2,4,8}; v2 labels them {2,4,6} but retains the old caption. These inconsistencies limit exact setting reconstruction. The horizon grid, metrics, and remaining stated protocol are retained.

E4.justification: The numerical study retains the same estimation, equilibrium-convergence, and regret questions. No separate ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study is added or removed; appendix Figures 3–5 remain mathematical illustrations.

E5.justification: Both versions report 35 independent simulation repetitions, average performance, and 95% confidence intervals. Changed plotted interval widths do not alter the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces numerical estimation-error, equilibrium-distance, and regret curves within the existing simulation study. For example, the largest-market row ends near 320 regret at T=1600 for N=8 in v1 and near 170 for N=6 in v2. These different configurations do not establish a same-setting gain; the broad convergence trends remain.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, theorem bounds, and appendix derivations are retained. Proposition 6.5 now explicitly displays the conditional center already defined in Appendix D, Equation (21). Other mathematical edits reconcile duplicate expressions or adjust typesetting without introducing new reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same semiparametric pricing contribution, equilibrium guarantees, concentration results, and stated T^(5/7) regret and T^(-1/7) price-convergence rates.

C2.justification: The explanations and limitations concerning common exploration, separate parameter/link estimation, known s-concavity parameters, and future joint estimation remain unchanged. No new substantive interpretation accompanies the revised simulation curves.

D1.justification: New Section 9.2 provides a GitHub repository address for simulation and figure code; v1 contains no corresponding access statement. This adds reproducibility information, although repository contents and functionality cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged. The positioning relative to linear competitive pricing, monotone single-index estimation, and shape-constrained inference is retained.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Optimal Nonlinear Online Learning under Sequential Price Competition via s-Concavity' to 'Revenue Maximization Under Sequential Price Competition Via The Estimation Of s-Concave Demand Functions'. v2 adds a short Supplement section, removes the acronym list, and makes localized explanatory and notation edits.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with revised axis ranges and an N=6 bottom-row label while retaining its three-by-four structure. The acronym table is removed, several equations are reformatted, and references and appendices reflow. Figure 1 and appendix Figures 3–5 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency by correcting the coefficient sign and revenue expression, makes Proposition 6.5 more self-contained, and adds simulation-code access information. These are useful but limited gains. The central theory and claims remain unchanged, and revised simulation values do not establish stronger evidence under comparable settings; Figure 2 still contains an inconsistent seller-count caption.
